resources.string: Relax app installation and update checks
Choose the core checks to relax below. Turning this off restores the original checks for new installs and keeps your selections.
Install an older version over a newer one without uninstalling it first.
Update an app with an APK signed by a different key; the app keeps its data.
Install modified APKs, v1-only APKs, or APKs with compressed resource tables.
Prohibit automatic recovery of modified content.
Install a base APK and its split APKs even when their signatures differ.

Extremely dangerous: allow differently signed apps to join the same ordinary app shared UID. They may share permissions and access each other’s private data, causing data leaks or app failures. Turning this off does not undo existing shared UID membership. System UIDs require the additional option below.
Extremely dangerous: also relax signature checks for system UIDs and privileged shared groups, including re-signed updates to their apps.

Extremely dangerous! Differently signed apps may join system or privileged shared groups such as android.uid.system and replace apps in those groups, including miui.systemui.plugin.

Untrusted code could gain system-level privileges, access sensitive data, crash the system UI, or prevent the device from booting normally.

Turning this off does not remove installed apps or shared UID membership, or restore original apps. Enable only if you understand the risks and have a recovery method. Whether an APK runs correctly still depends on compatibility with your system version.
Allow apps for older Android versions
Install apps that target an Android version the system normally blocks.
Do not ask the system verification service to check new installs.
Update apps that the system normally treats as always running.
Skip HyperOS restrictions on updating certain preinstalled apps.
Skip HyperOS checks based on install source or device rules.
